headline: South Asia: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict.
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran giving Yemen's Houthis target intelligence for drone, missile strikes on Saudi Arabia - report.
- Africa: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
The Army's 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated as the service reshapes its PSYOP and information warfare forces to counter global adversaries.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, one day ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE

- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russians attack Zaporizhstal for fifth time, firing six ballistic missiles – photo.
Russia has attacked the Zaporizhstal steelworks for the fifth time, firing six ballistic missiles at its energy, logistics and production facilities.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russians strike Sumy and Sumy Oblast with guided bombs: residential area hit, two injured – photos.
Russian forces attacked Sumy and Sumy Oblast with guided aerial bombs on Saturday morning, hitting a residential area and injuring two people.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Zelenskyy says Russia wants to deploy ballistic missile systems in Belarus to attack Ukraine's west.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated that Russia intends to deploy ballistic missile systems in Belarus to attack the western part of Ukraine.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Third Corps posts footage of first strike on Russia's new Dragon thermobaric weapon system.
Soldiers from the 3rd Army Corps have struck a Russian TOS-3 Drakon (Dragon) thermobaric rocket launcher system for the first time. The system was hit by a drone.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Wer führt in Zukunft die SPD? Mit Rasmus Buchsteiner.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Wer führt in Zukunft die SPD? Mit Rasmus Buchsteiner.
Es war eine Chaoswoche für den Kanzler Friedrich Merz. Das Rentenpaket entwickelt sich zur weiteren Zerreißprobe für die Koalition. Der neue Arbeitsminister Alexander Schweitzer macht es für den Kanzler nicht einfacher. Warum der SPD-Pragmatiker plötzlich auf Konfrontation geht und wie diese Machtkämpfe die Regierungsarbeit lähmen, steht im Zentrum der Analyse. Gleichzeitig brodelt es an der […]

- Jerusalem Post, 5 hours ago: Iran giving Yemen's Houthis target intelligence for drone, missile strikes on Saudi Arabia - report.

- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Russian strikes kill civilians, injure dozens across Ukraine.
At least eight people have been killed and nearly 60 injured in the latest wave of Russian strikes across Ukraine.
- Jerusalem Post, 3 hours ago: US lawmakers condemn settler violence after Washington Post journalist wounded in West Bank clashes.
While the Israeli condemnations largely called for further investigation to determine the facts, US and Palestinian condemnations accused Israeli settlers of having attacked Levine.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Sudan’s army claims dozens of RSF fighters killed in Nyala attack.
Rapid Support Forces accuse army of killing 30 civilians in attack on Nyala's busy livestock market.
Africa - bottom line: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit.
- Africanews, 5 hours ago: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit.
Iran has denied any involvement in an escalation of attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi targets. The international airport in Yemen’s interim capital Aden was struck by two missiles late on Friday, the second such incident in less than two weeks.
- Africanews, 22 hours ago: Ethiopian gains in Tigray risk wider war with Eritrea, analyst warns.
Ethiopia’s military advances in northern Tigray do not spell an end to the conflict but have the potential to increase the risk of war with neighboring Eritrea, an analyst with knowledge of the region has warned
- Africanews, 21 hours ago: Rights group says eastern Libyan authorities are carrying out executions.
Human Rights Watch says the military has killed an estimated 31 people since late August, with at least 50 other people at risk.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 20 hours ago: Uganda: MP Calls for Probe Into Recruitment of Ugandans to Fight for Russia.
[Nile Post] Rukiga County MP Patrick Katabaazi has asked the government to investigate reports that Ugandan youths are being recruited through deceptive job offers and deployed to fight for Russia in the war against Ukraine.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Media Statement - Defence Committee Calls for Urgent Action to Reverse SANDF Decline.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Media Statement - Defence Committee Calls for Urgent Action to Reverse SANDF Decline.
[Parliament of South Africa] The Portfolio Committee on Defence and Military Veterans has called for urgent intervention to reverse the decline of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF), warning that persistent resource shortages, financial pressures and governance weaknesses are undermining the country's defence capability.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
[Daily Maverick] On 15 October, former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O'Regan received the George Bizos Human Rights Award, reflecting on the project of democracy and urging resistance to rising authoritarianism.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: Zimbabwe: Poverty, Injustice Threaten Lasting Peace in Zimbabwe - ZPP.
[263Chat] The Zimbabwe Peace Project (ZPP) has called for greater investment in justice, human rights and inclusive institutions warning that poverty, inequality and weak access to justice continue to threaten lasting peace in Zimbabwe.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi rebels. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack last week. “We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue,” Araghchi said in a speech at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump.
President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine. The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped.
- The Hindu - International, Ukrainska Pravda, South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the U.S.-Russia diesel deal a “weak decision” that would help Moscow prolong the war, as Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed three children among the dead
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: North Korea says tested AI-assisted torpedo system.
North Korea has tested a “new-type” precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance, state media reported Saturday, as the nuclear-armed country steps up weapons testing. The announcement came days after Pyongyang said it had test-fired two types of cruise missiles from a submarine after weeks of friction with Seoul over a landmine explosion along their border.

Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz called the teacher’s actions “heroic” during a news conference and said she was not injured. He identified the attacker as 16-year-old Griffin J. In 1990, for example, its officials helped broker talks between Cambodia’s warring factions, supplementing international efforts to end conflict in the country. Now, Tokyo is seeking to upgrade its diplomatic toolkit. China’s embassy in Thailand has warned citizens to carefully plan their trips and pay extra attention to transport security following a string of high-profile kidnappings targeting Chinese nationals. Online influencers and artists were also advised to remain vigilant against high-paying job scams operating in Thailand in the latest such warning issued on Friday. India - bottom line: 'I love you' on clothes & a chilling note: What preceded Gurgaon techie couple's deaths.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 11 hours ago: 'I love you' on clothes & a chilling note: What preceded Gurgaon techie couple's deaths.
An IT professional, Mohammad Aslam, and his wife, Farhana, were discovered dead in their Gurgaon apartment. Aslam sent an alarming email to his employer before the incident, indicating a distressing situation. Police suspect that Aslam may have killed his wife before taking his own life. Relatives claim that Aslam had been struggling with depression for about 18 months prior to the tragedy.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Why Trump's plan to unleash 'Mother Of All Bombs' may fall flat in Iran.
Military discussions are considering the use of the MOAB against Iran's nuclear facilities and military targets. However, the effectiveness of the MOAB is limited against deeply buried sites protected by reinforced concrete. Analysts highlight that the GBU-57 penetrator is better suited for such underground facilities, which require specialized weapons for effective targeting. While the MOAB has a strong psychological impact, its military utility against hardened targets is questionable.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: "Will Be Crushed Under Weight Of Power": Pak Opposition Leader Warns Military.
Addressing a public gathering in Punjab's Multan district on Friday, Rehman said Pakistan could function effectively only when the military, bureaucracy and elected institutions operated within their respective constitutional domains.
